filing_playbook.action: Request a written zoning determination from the San Francisco Planning Department confirming whether a mobile food facility is permitted, conditional, or prohibited in C-2/Waterfront 2.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit a Letter of Determination request describing the food truck operation at 430 Beach St (C-2 zoning, Waterfront 2 SUD), stating that the rule table has no use category for mobile food facilities and the supplied pathway says a CUA is required but the basis is unclear. Ask Planning to confirm in writing whether a mobile food facility at this address is (1) principally permitted, (2) requires a Conditional Use Authorization under PC § 303, or (3) is prohibited, and to cite the specific code sections. Do not file any other applications or sign a lease until this answer is in hand.

filing_playbook.action: Register the business with the San Francisco Treasurer & Tax Collector (1–5 days, $55–$700 tiered by gross receipts) and file a Fictitious Business Name statement if the DBA differs from the legal entity name.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The registration year runs April 1 to March 31. Every other city department asks for the Business Account Number (BAN), so complete this immediately. File the FBN statement with the County Clerk, publish in a court-approved newspaper once a week for four weeks, and file proof of publication within 45 days.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

timeline_cost.notes: No time or cost range is given because zoning does not permit the concept as described at this address under the rule table: the table has no use category for mobile food facilities in C-2, so whether a food truck is allowed by right, requires conditional use authorization, or is prohibited is not established. The supplied pathway for April 2022 states a CUA is required, but the rule lines cite only 'unscreened open-air use' and 'Waterfront SUD' without showing how those triggers apply to a food truck. Obtain a written zoning determination from Planning before filing any applications. If Planning confirms a CUA is needed, budget 4–10 months (120–300 days) and $3,100–$15,000 for the CUA hearing, 1–3 months (30–90 days) and $880–$1,500 for the mobile food facility health permit, and 2–6 months (60–180 days) and $1,151–$5,000 per location for each Public Works location permit if the truck occupies public right-of-way (routinely appealed by nearby restaurants, so apply for multiple candidate locations). If Planning states the use is principally permitted, the CUA step and its 4–10 months drop out and the total shortens to 3–9 months for health and location permits. Zero precedent decisions for mobile food facilities exist in the records, so the CUA outcome and conditions cannot be predicted from comparable cases.

records_summary: 430 Beach St is in the C-2 (Community Business) zoning district within the Waterfront 2 Special Use District and the Priority Equity Geographies SUD on the Fisherman's Wharf tourist corridor. The site has operated as a limited restaurant and tea shop since at least 2018, with three health department referrals approved between 2018-01-29 and 2018-04-17. The immediate area is saturated with food businesses: 20 registered food or drink establishments and 11 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 ft (27 licenses within 1,000 ft), triggering the undue-concentration flag. Mobile food facilities are not covered by the Planning Code rule table, so the pathway analysis shows no use control was looked up and no change-of-use determination was made. The base rate shows zero dated use decisions for comparable businesses within 1,000 ft in the last 10 years (193 records were excluded as building work or agency referrals, and 30 were grant-only permits/licenses), so no approval rate can be calculated.
